### Trending products

### Top forum threads

What do you think? …

André J

Hi Product Hunt.  
  
For the past two years, we’ve been running AI agents against real production cloud infrastructure at CloudGeni. We learned the hard way that getting an agent to work once is only the beginning. Keeping it running, giving it somewhere safe to execute, connecting users’ accounts, getting human approval, and understanding what happened—and what it cost—is where the work adds up.  
  
We kept rebuilding that infrastructure. So we pulled it out and open-sourced it.

That’s Opengeni: agents in your product, infrastructure out of the box.

It gives developers the pieces they need to ship agents, already wired together: [...] 🔄 Sessions that survive errors, with a replayable history so you can reconnect and pick up where you left off.

🖥️ Sandboxes for agents to do the work, with credentials handled and memory built in.

🔌 Your APIs and your users’ apps, connected. Bring an OpenAPI or GraphQL spec, or an MCP server, plus 100+ integrations with built-in OAuth.

✋ Human approvals before risky actions, so people stay in control.

🔍 Visibility into every step, token, and dollar, with built-in dashboards and run traces.

🧩 A workspace for each customer and the freedom to choose your models.

Getting it into your product takes three steps: add your API key on the server, mount a handler using your existing authentication, and show the agent in your app—with your own UI or our React components. [...] If you don't want to stream, use our webhooks (turn.completed, session.requiresAction, etc.) and fetch the events when you need them. If you do stream, it picks up where you left off. And if you meant MCP, our MCP endpoints already use Streamable HTTP.

On serverless: the core itself doesn't scale to zero today. The workers are long-running and we deploy on Kubernetes or Native Cloud. Your own backend can totally be serverless though, since the SDK runs on edge runtimes. One tip: don't proxy the SSE stream through a function, it'll stay open and cost you. Webhooks are the cheaper way to go.   
  
More here: 

No public issue on this yet, feel free to open one! 

Yngve

results.title: Introducing OpenGeni: An Agentic Runtime for Organizations
results.content:
## Who this is for

 Platform teams building an internal developer platform where AI agents are first-class participants, not bolted-on copilots.
 SREs who want infrastructure agents to operate at the same level of governance their humans already do.
 Engineering leaders who want a path to safely scale AI adoption across the org, without each team reinventing credentials, sandboxing, and audit from scratch.
 Builders who've read the Infrastructure Agents Guide and want a working reference implementation to start from.

If you're a solo developer who wants your own agent, OpenClaw is probably what you want. If you're an org that wants AI to do real infrastructure work across multiple teams, multiple clouds, and multiple workflows, OpenGeni is built for you.

## Go run it [...] ## Go run it

The repo is live. MIT licensed. Self-hostable on your own infra, in your own cloud, with your own credentials.

→ github.com/Cloudgeni-ai/opengeni

If you want the same architectural layers without running them yourself, that's what Cloudgeni is for. But either way, the runtime should be solid. Build on it.

Found a gap? Have a workflow you wish OpenGeni shipped with? Open an issue or start a discussion on the repo. We're shipping fast and would rather hear from you now than later.
